newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 23.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 23.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Football League player Che Cockatoo-Collins says the AFL has not come far enough on the issue of on-field racial abuse after the sport introduced the Racial and Religious Vilification Code two years ago. The criticism came after this year's third case involving racial abuse was heard at the AFL Tribunal, where the Western Bulldogs' Steve Kolyniuk apologised to Melbourne's Jeff Farmer for abusive comments in their game on the weekend. Page 20.

Geelong player Gary Hocking will face the AFL Tribunal tonight for allegedly striking Essondon player Matthew Lloyd with an arm to the head during the weekend's match at the MCG. It is the second time Hocking has been ordered to appear in front of the juiciary this month. Page 20.

Disgraced Western Reds Super League captain Mark Geyer will take the unprecedented step of taking his seven-match suspension for eye-gouging to the New South Wales Supreme Court. The incident occurred at Geyer's first game back after serving a three-match suspension for a high tackle. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

The Commonwealth Bank ended its 17-year sponsorship of the schoolboys' rugby league Commonwealth Bank Cup competition, after a wild brawl marred a game between Camp Hill State High School and Clairvaux MacKilliop College last week. The brawl, which has rceived wide media coverage, resulted in 20 players form both teams receiving suspensions, ranging from one week to 12 months. Page 44.

New South Wales rugby union coach matt Williams says his Warratahs side is "ashamed" of its performance in last week's 26-16 loss to Queensland which has effectively ended the team's chance of making this year's semi-finals of the Super 12 competition. Wlliams has predicted an intense week of training in the lead up to this weekend's showdown with the ACT Brumbies. Page 44.

Australian cricket player Mark Waugh has engaged in a little pre-Ashes hype, labelling English cricket as "soft" and saying English players lacked hunger and toughness and did not play as a team. Waugh said the series could resemble 1993 when Australia won 4-1, unless Australia played below its best and England found some much needed form. Page 43.
THE AGE

Australian wheel-chair sensation Louise Savage added another trophy to her cabinet yesterday, winning the women's wheelchair section of the Boston marathon. Her win came after her main rival and seven times winner of the marathon, Jean Driscoll, overturnd when the pair were locked together only five kilometres from the finish. Page B14.

Leading Australian jockey Darren Beadman has turned down a lucrative chance to ride in England, preferring to stay in Australia and chase George Moore's record of 17 group one wins in a season. Beadman has 13 group one wins to his credit this season, andthere are thirteen more races remaining in Brisbane and Adelaide. Page B14.

Touring car driver Greg Murphy says he will not let a major crash he suffered two weeks ago disrupt his preparations for the third round of the championships next weekend. Murphy says he was lucky to escape with minor bruising when his Commodore speared off the track into the safety rail on the Phillip Island track. Page B14.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian basketball player Mark Bradke has returned to play for the Melbourne Tigers in the NBL after a troubled year-long stint playing for the Philadelphia 76ers in the US. Bradke, 28, says it was difficult to break into the team as a "veteran" rookie, but says he is glad he made the trip to the NBA, the best basketball competition in the world. Page 78.

Australians Sandon Stolle and Jason Stoltenburg advanced to the second round of the US clay court tennis championships in Orlando yesterday, with straight-sets victories. Little-known Argentinean Martin Rodriguez caused the biggest upset of the tournamen, beating second seed Malivai Washington 6-2, 6-2. Page 70.

The Australian Joeys under 17 soccer team beat the Solomon Islands 4-0 yesterday to book a place in the final in the Oceania qualifying group for the youth world cup. Coach Les Scheinflug said he was not completely satisfied with the team's performance, ut says the team has a very good chance of defeating long-time rivals New Zealand in the final. Page 70.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

New Zealand rugby league coach Frank Endacott has reignited ARL-Super League tensions, saying only four ARL players would make the current Australian Super League team. In the lead up to this week's Super League test match between the two countries, Endacott says only captain Brad Fitler, and Manly players Steve Menzies, Daniel Gartner and Nik Kosef could force their way into the Super League side. Page 68.

Australian softball pitcher Carolyn Crudington says she may have to resort to painkillers in her knee and back if she wants to take her place in the line-up for Australia's first game in the International Challenge which starts in Brisbane tonight. Crudigton was a standout for the bronze medal-winning Australian team in last year's Olympic Games. Page 63.

Australian rugby union coach Greg Smith said the clashes during the weekend match between Queensland and New South Wales which resulted in six citings and three suspensions did nothing for the image of the game, but said it will not affect camaraderie in he Australian team for the up-coming Bledisloe match against New Zealand. Page 62.
